explanation: For each ε>0, F is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of Dε, so Green's theorem applies with curl 2x−4y. Thus Γlim=limε→0 ∫ε¹∫ᵧ²⁻ᵧ(2x−4y)dx dy=∫₀¹4(1−y)(1−2y)dy=2/3. The logarithmic contributions on the sloping edges converge individually because ∫₀¹|ln(y)|dy is finite; on the horizontal truncated edge, dy=0. This proves the specified limit, while the original ordinary circulation remains undefined.

For $0<\epsilon<1$, let $C_\epsilon$ be the positively oriented (counterclockwise) boundary of $D_\epsilon=D\cap\{y\ge\epsilon\}$. Use Green's theorem on $D_\epsilon$ to evaluate the limiting circulation

$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{lim}}=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\oint_{C_\epsilon}F\cdot dr.$$

This explicit one-sided limit is the intended interpretation. The original ordinary line integral over the untruncated triangle is undefined because $\ln y$ is undefined on its entire bottom edge.
